body:
> I'm not familiar with C#, but this looks good to me. The logic for determining the line number doesn't quite match the GDScript plugin's for `Tr()` and `TrN()` calls (which can contain multiple translatable strings), but that's probably not a big deal.我不熟悉 C#，但这对我来说看起来不错。确定行号的逻辑与 GDScript 插件的 `Tr（）` 和 `TrN（）` 调用（可以包含多个可翻译字符串）不太匹配，但这可能没什么大不了的。

Could you provide some examples?

I'm using the following test case:
```csharp
using Godot;
using System;

public partial class Test : Node
{
    public override void _Ready()
    {
        #if TOOLS
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr1"));
        #endif
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr2", "ctx_a"));
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr3")); // NO_TRANSLATE
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr4")); // TRANSLATE: Message 4
        #if GODOT_ANDROID
            // TRANSLATE: Message 5
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr5"));
        #endif
            // Above comment.
            // TRANSLATE: Message 6 Line 1
            // Message 6 Line 2
            // Message 6 Line 3
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr6"));
            // Above comment.
            /* TRANSLATE: Message 7
             * Message 7 Line 2
             * Message 7 Line 3
             * Message 7 Line 4
             */
            GD.Print(TrN("Tr_n7", "Tr_n7_plural", 0, "ctx_b"));
        
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr8", "ctx_c")); // TRANSLATE: Message 8.1
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr8", "ctx_c")); // TRANSLATE: Message 8.1
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr8", "ctx_c")); // TRANSLATE: Message 8.2
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr8", "ctx_d")); // TRANSLATE: Message 8.3
            // TRANSLATE: Message 9
        
            // Empty line ^^
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr9"));
        
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr10")); // TRANSLATE: Message 10
            GD.Print(Tr("Tr11"));
    }
}
```
This is the corresponding generated .pot file:
```pot
# LANGUAGE translation for test for the following files:
# res://Test.cs
#
# FIRST AUTHOR <EMAIL@ADDRESS>, YEAR.
#
#, fuzzy
msgid ""
msgstr ""
"Project-Id-Version: test\n"
"MIME-Version: 1.0\n"
"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8-bit\n"

#: Test.cs:11
msgctxt "ctx_a"
msgid "Tr2"
msgstr ""

#. TRANSLATORS: TRANSLATE: Message 4
#: Test.cs:13
msgid "Tr4"
msgstr ""

#: Test.cs:22
msgid "Tr6"
msgstr ""

#. TRANSLATORS: TRANSLATE: Message 7
#. * Message 7 Line 2
#. * Message 7 Line 3
#. * Message 7 Line 4
#: Test.cs:29
msgctxt "ctx_b"
msgid "Tr_n7"
msgid_plural "Tr_n7_plural"
msgstr[0] ""
msgstr[1] ""

#. TRANSLATORS: TRANSLATE: Message 8.1
#. TRANSLATE: Message 8.2
#: Test.cs:31
#: Test.cs:32
#: Test.cs:33
msgctxt "ctx_c"
msgid "Tr8"
msgstr ""

#. TRANSLATORS: TRANSLATE: Message 8.3
#: Test.cs:34
msgctxt "ctx_d"
msgid "Tr8"
msgstr ""

#: Test.cs:38
msgid "Tr9"
msgstr ""

#. TRANSLATORS: TRANSLATE: Message 10
#: Test.cs:40
msgid "Tr10"
msgstr ""

#: Test.cs:41

msgstr ""

```

> Could you provide some examples?

I mean multiline calls like:

```gdscript
var test = tr_n(    # <-- The start line of the call.
    "tr_n7",        # <-- The start line of the first argument.
    "tr_n7_plural",
    0,
    "ctx_b",
)
```

In the case of GDScript, the line number containing the `tr_n()` call will be used, i.e., the `tr_n` identifier. In the case of C#, it's the line number of the first argument, as far as I understand. This isn't critical, and it's debatable which option is more correct. In the case of GDScript, the choice was probably justified by the fact that we cannot give preference to any of the arguments and therefore preferred the whole call (this only applies to `tr()` and `tr_n()`, in all other cases the starting line of the argument itself is used).

A much more important point is that if at least one of the arguments is non-constant, we skip the entire call:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/36b92128b1bce1f98687add98c84fd70ae9b20ca/modules/gdscript/editor/gdscript_translation_parser_plugin.cpp#L350

But as far as I understand, this is already done in the C# plugin as well?

> But as far as I understand, this is already done in the C# plugin as well?

As far as I know, yes, we already skip said calls in C# as well.

> This isn't critical, and it's debatable which option is more correct.

It shouldn't be too difficult to match GDScript on the line number, if we want to. I imagine the following also gives the `tr_n` line (and not the line containing the opening bracket)?
```gdscript
var test = tr_n
    ("tr_n7", "tr_n7_plural", 0, "ctx_b")
```
If we're fine with the discrepancy, I believe this can be merged.
